title: Building new drinks
lead: Every new drink starts from an old one. Change one part and taste.

sections.name: Swap one part

lines.label: In short
lines.text: Change the core, the balance or the seasoning.

know: Swap the spirit of an Old Fashioned for agricole rhum: a Ti’ Punch.
Swap its sugar for Bénédictine: a Monte Carlo.

Keep the total spirit the same.

A liqueur can be the sweetener, like the Sidecar’s orange liqueur.
A sweeter liqueur means less syrup.

sections.name: Write the spec

lines.label: In short
lines.text: If it isn’t written down, it isn’t a drink yet.

know: Amounts, glass, ice, method and garnish.
Build it three times the same way.
Name it so a guest can say it.

video.title: How to Invent your Own Cocktail w/ 3 Different Methods! | Cocktail Basics

keyPoints.line: an Old Fashioned with agricole rhum.
an Old Fashioned sweetened with Bénédictine.

read.bigIdea: New drinks are old drinks with one part changed.
read.where: Cocktail Codex’s six roots are templates. Keep the template and **swap one part**: the **core**, the **balance** or the **seasoning**. Swap the whiskey in an Old Fashioned for **agricole rhum** and you’re close to a **Ti’ Punch**. Swap its sugar for **Bénédictine** and you have a **Monte Carlo**.

stops.name: Seasoning
stops.text: Different **bitters**, a rinse, a new garnish.

read.mixup: Changing three things at once isn’t a riff, it’s a guess. Start with one.
read.sayIt: It’s built like an Old Fashioned, with rhum agricole instead of whiskey.

video.title: Dale DeGroff's Yummy Split Based Sazerac - Make it Quick

keyPoints.line: rye and Cognac, an ounce each.

read.bigIdea: Two spirits can share the core.
read.where: A **split base** uses two spirits where the root uses one. The **Vieux Carré** splits **rye and Cognac**, an ounce each, with sweet vermouth, Bénédictine and Peychaud’s. Keep the **total** spirit the same as the root, so the balance still works.
read.mixup: A split base isn’t more spirit. It’s the same amount, shared.
read.sayIt: It’s split between rye and Cognac, so it’s spicy and round at once.

video.title: GOLD RUSH - Whiskey Sour x Bees Knees (ONLY 3-ingredients!)

keyPoints.line: a Whiskey Sour with honey syrup.
can be the sweet part, like the Sidecar’s.

read.bigIdea: The sweet part can carry flavor.
read.where: Plain syrup only sweetens. A flavored sweetener sweetens **and** adds taste. Our **Gold Rush** is bourbon, lemon and **honey syrup**: a Whiskey Sour with honey. In the **Sidecar** family, an **orange liqueur** does the sweetening. When the new sweetener is sweeter, use **less**, and taste.
read.mixup: Adding a liqueur on top of the syrup makes a drink sweeter. Take some syrup out.
read.sayIt: It’s a whiskey sour sweetened with honey instead of sugar.

video.title: How to create your own Cocktail - Masterclass

keyPoints.line: the same way before it’s done.
it so a guest can say it.

read.bigIdea: A drink isn’t real until anyone can build it.
read.where: Write the **spec** like ours: every **amount**, the **glass**, the **ice**, the **method** and the **garnish**. Build it **three times** the same way; if it tastes different each time, the spec isn’t finished. Give it a **name** a guest can say out loud, and one line that sells it.
read.mixup: “A splash” isn’t an amount. Write the measure.
read.sayIt: It’s our own: we built it here and it’s only on our menu.

sources: Cocktail Codex (Alex Day, Nick Fauchald and David Kaplan, Ten Speed Press, 2018), as summarized by the publisher (randomhousebooks.com) and reviews; Our book: the classic cocktail specs in this app. Checked Nov 8, 2026.
